solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pastry first seen in Polynesian island group

indicators.note: in places the selected letter inside the group of islands named next

parts.note: Samoa is an island group in Polynesia

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: A traveller tastes a new pastry on a South Sea island.
explanation.walkthrough: The S goes into SAMOA after its third letter, giving SAMOSA.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried triangular Indian pastry with a spiced savoury filling.

clue.text: Rank material on one set of books

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing twill fabric
the New Testament is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Cloth is laid over a pile of ledgers, smelling bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' reads as smelly in the surface, but it is a military grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned officer's grade in the army or police.

clue.text: Utter a curse to Frenchman about citadel

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for monsieur

indicators.note: about here means turned around and scattered, so the letters of the fortress word are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a Frenchman over a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: To maledict is an archaic verb meaning to call down evil upon someone, the opposite of bless.

clue.text: Hid on isle in south-east Germany

indicators.note: in places the island inside the compass direction and country letters

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: Someone hid on an island in a corner of Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south-east Germany' looks like a region, but it is two abbreviations split around the island.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it or stash it away out of sight, so it matches hid.

clue.text: He may get high on his horse

definitions.text: He may get high on his horse

parts.words: He may get high on his horse
parts.note: surface reading: a proud rider sitting up high in the saddle
setter's reading: horse is slang for heroin, so this person gets high on a narcotic

explanation.walkthrough: 'On his high horse' is the idiom for being haughty, which steers you towards arrogance; horse is street slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes narcotics such as heroin to get intoxicated is an addict or habitual taker.

clue.text: Genuine manuscript showing spheres of activity

explanation.surface: An authentic manuscript reveals someone's fields of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are domains or fields in which a person or thing is active or has influence.

clue.text: Indian horse-drawn vehicle will worry German first

parts.note: to harry is to harass or worry

explanation.surface: A carriage in India is threatened by a German taking the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' simply places the abbreviation before the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A gharry is a horse-drawn cab or carriage formerly common in India and Egypt.

clue.text: O'Casey at church meeting

parts.note: Sean O'Casey was an Irish playwright
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The playwright attends a gathering at church.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a gathering of people trying to contact the dead, a particular sort of session.

clue.text: Creature's home covered in rubbish

indicators.note: covered in means one word is wrapped by another, sitting inside it

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair or a cosy room

explanation.surface: An animal's lair is buried under refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodent such as a rat or mouse is a gnawing mammal, one kind of animal.

clue.text: Widow having keepsake close to heart

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

explanation.surface: A bereaved wife holds a memento close to her heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Relict is an old legal and literary word for a woman whose husband has died.

clue.text: State three times and another — places remote from reality

definitions.note: plural definition for a singular idiom; any such place is la-la land

parts.note: LA is Louisiana, written three times
ND is North Dakota, a further US state

explanation.surface: Someone repeats a statement three times and then adds one more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb, to say, but it is an American state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: La-la land is an idiom for a dreamy fantasy world where people are out of touch with the real one.

clue.text: Some poured diesel on troubled waters

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters within them

parts.note: the run starts at the end of poured and continues into diesel

explanation.surface: Fuel is spilled onto choppy water, a twist on pouring oil on troubled waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddies are swirling currents of water running against the main flow, so water that is disturbed.

clue.text: Hank or Chuck, say, turning round in camera

indicators.note: turning round suggests the letters are spun into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Two people are filmed while spinning about.
explanation.walkthrough: Hank and Chuck are typical US first names, and 'in camera' is a legal phrase meaning in private.
explanation.definitionFit: Hank and Chuck are given as examples of typical men from the United States.

clue.text: A leading tutor with terribly poor student to start with — that's fate!

indicators.note: terribly signals that the next word is badly mangled into a new order
leading picks out the letter at the front of the word that follows
to start with keeps only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A top tutor teaching a weak student exclaims at his destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the three Fates spun, measured and cut the thread of life; Atropos was the one who cut it.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropos is one of the three Fates of Greek mythology, the goddess who severs each life's thread.

clue.text: Indication of ownership during Whitsuntide

indicators.note: during means within the following word, so the letters sit inside it

parts.note: letters two to four of the word

explanation.surface: Someone shows they own something at Whitsun, the Christian festival of Pentecost.
explanation.definitionFit: Its is the possessive form of it, a grammatical marker that something belongs to a thing.

clue.text: Steal the Spanish metal

parts.note: British slang: to nick is to pinch
el is the Spanish definite article

explanation.surface: A thief makes off with Spanish metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickel is a silvery-white metallic chemical element used in alloys and coins.

clue.text: Some sliding top

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the next word is used, a run inside it

parts.note: letters two to four of the word

explanation.surface: Part of a roof or cover slides open.
explanation.definitionFit: A lid is a removable cover for a box or pot, the piece that closes it from above.

clue.text: At cards, one is very good

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the playing card ranked as one
second meaning: excellent, top-notch, in informal use

explanation.surface: A card player is praised for being excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the single-pip playing card and also serves as slang for first-rate.

clue.text: End of the match?

parts.note: surface reading: the final whistle of a sporting fixture
setter's reading: a match is also a marriage, and this is how one legally ends

explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' points at sport, but a match is also a couple, a good marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorce is the legal dissolution of a marriage, ending the union of husband and wife.

clue.text: Cut of meat, peas and cole served

indicators.note: served suggests dished up in a fresh arrangement on the plate

parts.note: taken as written; cole is cabbage

explanation.surface: A plate of meat comes with peas and cabbage on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin boneless slice of meat, often veal, beaten flat and fried.

clue.text: Deadpan comedian, we hear, saw off birds

indicators.note: we hear means the comedian's name is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: Jack Dee is a British comedian known for his lugubrious, deadpan style; his surname sounds like the letter D

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong, so the letters of the cutting tool are jumbled

explanation.surface: A glum comic took a saw to some birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackdaws are small grey-naped members of the crow family, common birds in Britain.

clue.text: Ruins of Dorset, scattered heartlessly — yes!

indicators.note: scattered tells you the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: the English county, taken as written

indicators.note: without its heart a word loses its middle, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone cheers at ancient ruins spread across the county of Dorset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruins of Dorset' reads as a noun phrase, but ruins is a verb here, and 'heartlessly' attaches to the yes after the dash.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy something is to wreck it completely, the same as the verb ruins in the third person.

clue.text: House and grounds from Eastern Maine, say

parts.note: Maine is an example of a US state

explanation.surface: A property with land is in the east of Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large country property consisting of a mansion with its surrounding land.

clue.text: They could be square or round balls

definitions.text: They could be square or round
definitions.meaning: first meaning: square ... and round ... are kinds of folk dancing
second meaning: formal social occasions for dancing

explanation.walkthrough: Square and round seem to describe the shape of balls, but each names a style of folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls are formal parties held for dancing, and square and round are named styles of that activity.

clue.text: Dared cold gal to take off clothing and nipple ring

indicators.note: removing the clothing strips each word of its outer letters, leaving its inner part

explanation.surface: A girl is dared to strip in the cold, revealing a piercing.
explanation.definitionFit: The areola is the ring of pigmented skin surrounding the nipple.

clue.text: Just over five hundred vehicles in Beds?

parts.note: 501 in Roman numerals is D plus I

explanation.surface: About five hundred vans are parked in Bedfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' looks like the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county; the question mark flags that it is plain furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Divans are low backless beds or couches, a common type of bed base.

clue.text: It's 5p now to bounce gently up and down

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a shilling, worth five new pence after decimalisation
second meaning: to move up and down, as on water

explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the old British shilling, twelve old pence, equal to five pence in today's money.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is old slang for the pre-decimal shilling coin and also a verb for bobbing on water.

clue.text: Just the VW car for a drive!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Volkswagen's famous rounded small model
second meaning: a ... is also a heavy mallet, so to ... is to drive in with one

explanation.surface: A Volkswagen Bug is the ideal car for an outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A drive' reads as an outing in the car, but the verb sense is driving wedges or pegs with a heavy mallet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Volkswagen Beetle is the classic VW model, and to beetle is to pound or drive with a mallet.

clue.text: Israeli male ordered travellers' rewards

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are sorted afresh

explanation.surface: An Israeli man booked a trip and earned points.
explanation.definitionFit: Air miles are loyalty points collected on flights and purchases and redeemed for trips.

clue.text: Mum rearranged trek to bazaar

indicators.note: rearranged plainly says the letters of the hike word are put in another order

explanation.surface: Mother changed her plans and walked to the bazaar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is an oriental marketplace of stalls, so the two are near synonyms for a trading place.

clue.text: About to marry anew in sea area

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: anew means done over in a fresh form, so the letters before it are refashioned

explanation.surface: A couple plan to remarry at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromarty is one of the sea areas named in the BBC Shipping Forecast, off north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromarty is a named stretch of water in the British Shipping Forecast, off Scotland's east coast.

clue.text: Salad ingredient also covered coaster

indicators.note: covered means one word wraps around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a coaster is a small table mat

explanation.surface: A slice of salad is also sitting on a drinks coaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaster' suggests a ship or rollercoaster; it is a mat under a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomatoes are a red fruit commonly sliced into salads as a raw ingredient.

clue.text: Turning northeastwards, missing out Harrow and airport

indicators.note: turning suggests what is left is twisted round into a new order
missing out means the letters of the tool word are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: the farm implement, or the London school, taken as written to be removed

explanation.surface: A traveller heads north-east, bypassing Harrow, towards the airport.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking H, A, R, R, O and W out of NORTHEASTWARDS leaves NTESTADS; Harrow is a district of north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Stansted is London's third airport, in Essex to the north-east of the capital.

clue.text: Contacts the French about three points

indicators.note: about means the French article goes around the other letters, surrounding them

parts.note: les is the French plural definite article
three compass points: east, north, south

explanation.surface: A French person is phoned about three issues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contacts' looks like a verb, getting in touch; it is the noun for eye lenses.
explanation.definitionFit: Contacts are contact lenses, thin discs of plastic worn on the eye to correct vision.
